::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 9th 1895  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear [Sir](people/person_1652.qmd)[^1]
The kindness of your letter to me emboldens me to send you some observations on the present state of criticism with my name.[^2] I have done a good deal of criticism and was for many years an editor besides what I have endured as an author and I can certainly declare that former criticism was really useful to me while what I see now can do good to no one except as an advertisement. I have long wished to protest against spoiling stories by composing to satisfy magazine

Yours truly
C M Yonge		

I hope your attack of the pestilence has passed off as well as mine has.

---

[^1]: Besant was knighted in the Queen’s Birthday Honours this year (24 May 1895).
[^2]: Possibly for publication in the *Author*, the organ of the Society of Authors, edited by Besant.
